subject: URGENT: Production streaming header corruption causing elevated errors / latency
messages:
From: Todd Mercer <todd.mercer@acmehealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Production errors and latency spikes - streaming responses

Diego / Marissa,

We started seeing a spike in 5xx errors and very long tail latency on our integrations with your streaming endpoint around 14:55 UTC. Our telemetry shows a sudden increase in streaming parser failures, followed by repeated client reconnects. Samples attached (error_samples.log and a short pcap).

Impact: many transactions failing during peak clinical sync (latency > 5s, error rate ~8% for the last 15 minutes). This is affecting our EHR sync SLA.

Can you triage urgently? If there's a temporary mitigation (fallback to non-streaming or disable a particular header), we need that ASAP. We will open an incident on our side as well.

Thanks,
Todd Mercer
Lead Integration Engineer
Acme Health

--
Attachment: error_samples.log (text), client-pcap-snippet.txt (pcap excerpt)
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Todd Mercer <todd.mercer@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 15:26:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Production errors and latency spikes - streaming responses

Todd,

Thanks for the quick heads up and the attachments — appreciate the pcap. We're treating this as high priority. Initial notes from our on-call:
- We see a pattern that looks like header reassembly failures in the client SDK when callers use chunked metadata headers combined with intermittent keep-alives.
- That can occasionally result in the server closing the stream with a 5xx and the client retrying, which explains the reconnect storm and latency tail.

Immediate mitigations we can try:
1) Temporary route for your account to a model variant that disables streaming chunked-metadata (fast to flip, short-lived).
2) Short-term suggestion on your side: disable streaming mode for critical EHR sync windows until we stabilize (we'll help script the switch).

I'll loop in Karthik (SDK runtime) to start a deeper investigation and pull traces. Marissa, can you help coordinate a postmortem and customer exec comms if needed?

Diego
Diego Fernandez
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

> > We started seeing a spike in 5xx errors and very long tail latency on our integrations with your streaming endpoint around 14:55 UTC...
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Todd Mercer <todd.mercer@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Production errors and latency spikes - streaming responses

Diego / team,

Quick engineering triage notes:
- Reproduced a similar failure in a staging harness when we simulate chunked metadata headers interleaved with prefix caching. The client's streaming parser (v1.4.2) can mis-handle header boundaries on fragmented frames, producing a malformed header that our runtime treats as protocol error.
- Root cause appears to be a regression introduced in the SDK's framing fix (v1.4.0 -> v1.4.2) that tried to optimize header concatenation for memory but didn't account for mid-frame keep-alives.

Planned next steps:
- Push hotfix to SDK (v1.4.3) that adds robust boundary checks (ETA 3h).
- Server-side workaround: add tolerant parsing path for affected accounts and enable an automatic header reassembly guard for 24h to stop the immediate 5xxs (requires deploy + config flip, ETA 90m).
- I'll post a reproduction test and a patch diff to JIRA RINF-1209 in the next 30 minutes.

For Acme: Diego, recommend we flip the server-side guard immediately and provide the SDK patch + rollout instructions for their teams. We should also schedule a brief joint deploy window so Acme can upgrade to v1.4.3.

Karthik
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime

> On Wed, 21 Apr 2027 at 15:26 Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai> wrote:
> > Thanks for the quick heads up and the attachments — appreciate the pcap...
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Todd Mercer <todd.mercer@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 16:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Production errors and latency spikes - streaming responses

Diego / Karthik,

Thanks for the rapid triage. I'm escalating this to my director and Sales Ops because Acme is citing potential SLA penalties if this continues. Drafting an exec summary for them now. Proposed customer comms (short):
- Acknowledge impact and that we have an active mitigate + permanent fix plan.
- Expected timeline: server-side guard in 90m, SDK hotfix in ~3h, full rollout and verification in 24h.
- Offer a credit request form link and a 1:1 remediation review after postmortem.

Grace, can you prepare the postmortem template and collect traces for RINF-1209? Also please add the account to the dedicated mitigation routing so we can reduce blast radius.

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

> On Wed, 21 Apr 2027 at 16:05 Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> > Quick engineering triage notes:...
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Todd Mercer <todd.mercer@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 19:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Production errors and latency spikes - streaming responses

Update: server-side guard enabled for Acme (config flip completed at 18:35 UTC). Early telemetry shows error rate back down to baseline (~0.4%) and tail latency improved.

Karthik's SDK hotfix has been pushed (v1.4.3) and a patched client build is available in the Acme support drive. We're coordinating a rolling upgrade recommendation for their integration team; we advised keeping streaming disabled for the next 2 hours while they validate.

Next steps:
- Marissa: send the formal customer update and offer the credit form + postmortem invite.
- Karthik & Grace: retain traces, produce RCA in RINF-1209, and include reproduction steps for the SDK issue and the JTAC notes for future preventative tests.
- Diego: I'll prepare an exec note for leadership summarizing impact, actions, and recommended compensation if the customer requests it (cc devops and legal if needed).

Diego Fernandez
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
